excerpt: FlexChords is a web app that turns a YouTube video or audio file into synced guitar chords, with key and tempo detection and a chord editor. What's free, alternatives and launch feedback.
content:
FlexChords is a web app for guitarists. Paste a YouTube link or upload an audio file (WAV, MP3, M4A or FLAC) and it detects the chords, the key and the tempo, then shows the chords in time with the song so you can play along. A timeline lets you jump to any part of the song, and a chord editor lets you change a chord, move its start or end, split or delete it, with undo and redo. You can export the chords as timestamped labels for Audacity, Reaper and other audio editors.

The maker says a deep-learning model predicts the chords and a separate music-theory smoothing step removes the rapid, glitchy chord changes raw models tend to produce. Songs other people have already analysed sit in a public catalogue you can play along to for free, and a free account gets five new analyses a month.

FlexChords was built by Amit S Namboothiry, who describes himself as a guitarist, and launched on Product Hunt on 4 October 2026, finishing #20 for the day with 69 upvotes.

We have not tested FlexChords ourselves. This page brings together its official site, its Product Hunt page and the official pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.os: Runs in the browser; sign in with Google, email or phone
profile.starts_at: Free account: 5 song analyses a month; paid pricing not published
profile.summary_short: Web app that turns a YouTube video or audio file into synced guitar chords with key and tempo
use_cases: Learning a song from its YouTube video with the chords scrolling in time
Working out the key and tempo of a track before a jam or a cover
Fixing a detected chord sheet by hand on the timeline
Exporting chord labels into Audacity or a DAW for practice or arranging

paragraphs: Amit S Namboothiry says he built FlexChords out of two frustrations as a guitarist: chord charts for YouTube songs that were in the wrong key or heavily simplified, and chord-detection sites that put play-along, tempo and transposing tools behind subscriptions.

His focus at launch was accuracy. Raw machine-learning chord models jitter between chords, he wrote, so FlexChords adds a rule-based music-theory layer that smooths those glitches out and takes the song's key into account. He called the product a work in progress, said MIDI export was coming, and asked users for feedback on chord accuracy.
launch_story.attribution: Amit S Namboothiry, maker, on Product Hunt

fit: play guitar and learn songs from YouTube
want chords that follow the song as it plays, without paying first
use Audacity, Reaper or another audio editor and want chord markers on the timeline
not_fit: need tempo or transposition controls: we found neither in the app on 14 October 2026, although the site's description mentions them
need more than five new song analyses a month: no paid plan or price has been published yet
want a phone app or live microphone input: FlexChords runs in the browser and works from links and files

pricing.intro: Pricing not published. FlexChords has no pricing page. The app itself describes what a free account includes.

plans.name: Free account
plans.detail: 5 new song analyses a month (the count resets monthly); unlimited play-along for songs already in the catalogue and songs you have analysed

notes: The app's code refers to a "Pro" plan with unlimited analyses, but no price, sign-up or billing terms are shown anywhere. We will add it when it is published.
The site has no published terms of service or privacy policy as of 14 October 2026.

alternatives.intro: Chordify is on Product Hunt's alternatives list; Moises and Chord ai are closely comparable tools we added. Prices are what each product's own site states, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: Chordify
items.what: Chord detection for songs with play-along chord diagrams
items.starts_at: Free tier; see its Premium page for prices
items.difference: A long-established, catalogue-based service with a paid Premium tier. Its Premium page blocked our automated check, so we have not quoted a price.

items.name: Moises
items.what: Musician's toolkit with stem separation, a chord finder, speed changer and lyric transcription, on web, desktop and mobile
items.starts_at: Free tier with limited uploads a month; full pricing shown after login
items.difference: A broad suite with native apps. FlexChords does one job, guitar chords, in the browser.

items.name: Chord ai
items.what: Mobile app that detects chords and beats from YouTube, audio files or the phone's microphone
items.starts_at: Free to download; the site mentions a paid full version without a price
items.difference: Works on iOS and Android and can listen live through the microphone; FlexChords is browser-only.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Riffstation, SoundGate Guitar, Guitar Wiz, Chord Mini and Fretello, plus music generators such as Suno that do a different job.

liked: Accuracy across most songs one tester tried, including correct key detection
criticised: Chords that flip between major and minor on blues-style songs (an E and Em back-and-forth on ZZ Top's "Legs")
US phone numbers formatted wrongly at sign-in (the maker said a fix was coming)

quotes.text: I tried it on a few songs and it was pretty good in most cases.
quotes.author: Tyler Cutshall

quotes.text: It detected the key correctly (E) but the chord progression "ping-ponged" between E and Em.
quotes.author: Tyler Cutshall

pros: Free to use for catalogue songs, plus five new analyses a month
Works from any YouTube link or an uploaded audio file
Chord editor with undo and redo for fixing detections
Exports timestamped chord labels for Audacity and other audio editors
Detects key and tempo as well as chords
cons: No published price for heavier use
No terms of service or privacy policy published on the site
Blues-style songs can confuse the major and minor detection, as one early tester found
No tempo or transposition controls found yet, and MIDI export is still to come

x.none: We found no posts about FlexChords on X yet.

faq.a: Yes, for now. A free account gets five new song analyses a month, and songs already in the catalogue can be played along to without using any. No paid plan has been priced publicly.
A YouTube link, or an audio file in WAV, MP3, M4A or FLAC format.

We have not measured it. One early tester on Product Hunt found it good on most songs but saw it switch between E and Em on a blues track; the maker said he would work on those transitions. You can correct any chord in the editor.
Yes, as timestamped labels for Audacity, Reaper and other audio editors. The maker said MIDI export was coming soon at launch; we did not find it in the app on 14 October 2026.

faq.q: Can it transpose a song or slow it down?
faq.a: We did not find transposition or playback-speed controls in the app on 14 October 2026, although the site's description mentions them.

sources.label: Product Hunt page and launch discussion
